notes.1: The printed heading is VIIII. Full pages60–62 show alternating insets throughout this poem; these are source layout, not an assumption from verse parity.
notes.3: The source spells Elegeia, including the additional e, and ends the verse with an exclamation mark.
notes.4: The exclamation mark follows A; the verse ends with a colon.
notes.6: The source spelling is extructo. Corpus inane is set off with commas.
notes.9: The source reads Adspice, demissis ut eat miserabilis alis; the spelling and word order are retained.
notes.19: The printed forms inportuna here and inicit at20 are retained without normalization.
notes.21: The source has Ismario and Orpheo. The verse and the next end in question marks.
notes.23: The source names Linon and sets aelinon! inside quotation marks; no Greek spelling is substituted.
notes.25: Maeoniden is the printed name, followed by a quo ceu fonte perenni.
notes.35: The parenthesis contains ignoscite fasso!, including the exclamation mark. The comma after bonos precedes the opening parenthesis.
notes.37: The source has a colon after pius, a semicolon after moriere and another colon after sacra.
notes.43: The printed reading is Aurea sanctorum potuissent templa deorum, retained as written.
notes.47: The source prints Phaeacia. Verse49 has fugientis, not a supplied normalized ending.
notes.55: The speech uses a closed quotation after felicius, then inquit outside it, and resumes at amata through verse56. The separate quotation marks are retained schematically.
notes.57: The speech sets quid in its own quotation, with ait outside, then continues from tibi to the end of58. No comma is supplied before ait.
notes.60: The source has Elysia and ends the verse with a colon.
notes.63: The printed contraction falsumst is retained, as are tuast and siquast at65.
notes.64: The source has no comma between Galle and tuae; the verse ends with a period.
notes.68: The last verse ends in an exclamation mark. Heading X. and the next poem begin below it on printed page62, establishing this poem's boundary.
